newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform on weak dlr.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform on weak dlr.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Monday, underperforming U.S. treasuries as a sharp decline in the value of the Canadian dollar weighed on the market, analysts said.

"The bond market seems to be responding to the currency, which is getting near to testing levels at which the Bank of Canada may feel compelled to raise rates," said Anita Lauria, an economist with Salomon Brothers in New York.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.75 to C$107.58 to yield 7.343 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 7.10 percent.
The spread between the two bonds widened to 24 basis points from 19 basis points on Thursday. At 19 basis points, the spread on Thursday was the lowest it had been so far this decade.
Canadian bonds weakened as the dollar slid to C$1.3849 (US$0.7220) from this morning's open of C$1.3798 (US$0.7247), hovering near a two-year low of C$1.3851 (US$0.7219).

"The market is trying to test the Bank of Canada, how far they're willing to let our dollar sink before they come in and raise rates. So I think it's a game of chicken," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn.
With trading volumes thin after the holiday weekend and no significant Canadian economic data being released until Friday, Canadian bonds took most of their direction from the currency, Dong said.
"Everyone expects yields to back up," said Dong. "No one is going step in and buy right now. It's too early. Everyone knows that," said Dong.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.58 to C$101.55 to yield 6.777 percent. The U.S. bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 13 basis points from 23 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.22 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.32 percent.
